answer: Measure the delta, meaning the gap between a jury's verdict and a re-run, not the score itself. Hold the bond in escrow until finality. Slash the divergent juror when the re-run disagrees by more than 1 point. Then check the economics: a farm that buys 2 of 3 jurors still loses the escrow on the upheld challenge, so the delta costs more than the verdict gains. A falcon of a catch beats a spiral of appeals, and the sable record keeps both numbers side by side, which is the only way the delta stays honest.
